tasks.prompt: Summarise, in three or four sentences, how long a Python feature version is supported after its x.0 release and what kind of releases it gets in each phase, as the policy stands today.

rubric.text: Each feature series is maintained for five years in total, with the final source-only release five years after x.0.
For Python 3.13 and newer, the first two years (24 months) are full support with bugfix releases including installers, roughly every other month.
For 3.13 and newer, the remaining three years (36 months) get security fixes only, as source-only releases with no fixed cadence.
Python 3.9 to 3.12 keep the older calendar: 18 months of full support followed by 3½ years of security fixes.
There is no extended long-term support beyond the five years, as Python 2.7 had.

tasks.author: ai-task-writer-g
